problem: Provide recreation and physical activity space in a dense city.
title: Bogota closes main streets to cars every Sunday and holiday for people
context: Bogota ran a Ciclovia programme closing about 100 km of streets 72 times a year.
decision_made: Close main streets to motor traffic on Sundays and holidays for walking, cycling and exercise.
action_taken: Run by Bogota's sports institute; an economic analysis compared four Ciclovia programmes.
observed_outcome: A 2012 study found a cost-benefit ratio of 3.23 to 4.26 for Bogota, at about US $6.0 per capita per year, and surveys found most participants met leisure physical activity recommendations (59.5 percent).
lessons: Low-cost recurring street closures can deliver health benefits relative to cost.
limitations: The start date is reported as 1974 in one source and not confirmed for 1976. Estimates depend on programme directors' inputs and local surveys.

sources.publisher: American Journal of Public Health (via PMC)

claims.claim_text: Bogota's Ciclovia takes place 72 times a year on nearly 100 kilometres of streets.
The economic analysis reported a cost-benefit ratio of 3.23 to 4.26 for Bogota.
